title: How Wisdom Became the Property of the Human Race
source: Barker & Sinclair, West African Folk-Tales (1917), tale II
lesson: Sometimes the smallest voice is the wisest.
lines: Why is wisdom spread all over the world? Because Anansi dropped a pot. Father Anansi had all the wisdom in the world, and everyone came for advice.
But one day the people offended him. I'll take it all back!
He gathered every bit of wisdom into one great pot, sealed it, and set off to hide it at the top of the tallest tree.
But his son, Kweku Tsin, followed him.
Anansi hung the pot round his neck, in front, and began to climb. The pot swung. He slipped. The pot bumped his knees.
At last Kweku Tsin called, Father, why not hang the pot on your back? Anansi froze. I thought I had all the wisdom… but my son has more.
In a temper, he flung the pot down. It smashed on a rock, and wisdom spread throughout the world. Sometimes the smallest voice is the wisest.
